suggestions.title: "The study authors suggested the dosing may have been too low, or ..."
suggestions.reading: your skin-gel paragraph with this sentence: [Human Written, 0%](https://www.pangram.com/history/aa293ceb-d603-4fe1-9007-2ddc9c6a72bb), one window, High.
suggestions.why: You wrote "or it works better for generalized rather than focal seizures". The paper doesn't say "generalized": it says the doses may have been too low, and that the response in adults with focal epilepsy "is not as robust as seen in patients with Dravet syndrome" ([O'Brien et al. 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9270696/)). So it now reads "or that CBD just doesn't work as well for focal seizures as it does in Dravet syndrome, where many of the seizures are generalized." Your next sentence holds and stays: drug-induced seizures are generalized ones ([a toxicology teaching note](https://cumming.ucalgary.ca/sites/default/files/teams/127/pearl-ofthe-week/Drug%%20induced%%20seizure%%20Mar%%2015%%202019.pdf): "Drug induced seizures are generalized processes"), and with MDMA they often come from low sodium swelling the brain ([Merck Manual](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/special-subjects/illicit-drugs-and-intoxicants/methylenedioxymethamphetamine)). The 7-OH-CBD point is out, as you said.

suggestions.title: The focal-seizure sentence, out of the oral CBD paragraph
suggestions.reading: the paragraph without it: [Human Written, 0%](https://www.pangram.com/history/5d3d05f7-30aa-4aef-b6cf-08deb2f4bd96), one window, High (the cut sentence had been a Low window).
suggestions.why: You asked "why are we talking about focal seizures, when seizures from mdma and psychedelic overdoses are generalized seizures, right?" Right, and that question also applies to the last sentence of this paragraph, "For focal seizures outside those syndromes, the evidence is mixed, but still long-term." It's gone, so the paragraph ends on the syndromes your reader's case is closest to (in Lennox-Gastaut the most common seizures are generalized tonic ones: [MedLink](https://www.medlink.com/article/generalized_onset_tonic_seizures)). The skin-gel paragraph keeps its focal point, because that says why the trial may not apply.

suggestions.title: "I also read on forums that some people swear smoking at the aura ..."
suggestions.reading: four tries, all AI Detected: your version [62%](https://www.pangram.com/history/2419edef-dd6d-4c05-9ed3-32bf737bef33) (Human Low, AI Medium, AI Low); mine after the making-sense read [43%](https://www.pangram.com/history/fd1df50a-5f61-44ee-ad14-ab61bda0542c) (the first two sentences Human, the last two AI Low); after two readers' notes [98%](https://www.pangram.com/history/d3ff8463-b3c1-40f3-8852-d81cedc403ed); and this one, [41%](https://www.pangram.com/history/bbaa0976-fd6a-4cdb-bcb0-207e5e9d1265) (Human Low, then AI Low on the last two sentences).
suggestions.why: What I fixed for sense: "it" now says smoking at the aura (after the nasal-spray paragraph it could mean the spray); the EEG woman was in a published study ([Sivakumar et al. 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27763968/)), not on a forum; and the ending said "the THC may be what makes it go either way. That's what happened in rats", but in the rats THC only made it worse and CBD helped, so it now says "So it may come down to how much THC is in it". The last two sentences still read AI. The readers' notes ([PANEL.md](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261103/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h06-checks-20261105/panel-F2/PANEL.md)) both point at the ending as a tidy wrap-up and at the rat sentence's mirrored halves; rewording those without changing what they say made it worse.
